mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4% over two consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand and earnings pressure, which reduces corporate profit growth and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when UNRATE > 4.0 for two months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of two consecutive quarterly GDPC1 declines (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the federal funds rate above 5% over three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when FEDFUNDS > 5.0 for three months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in payroll employment above 200,000 new jobs per month over three consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 200,000 for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of three consecutive months with PAYEMS increases > 200,000 (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above 1.0% over three consecutive months signals strengthening manufacturing activity and economic growth, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of three consecutive months with INDPRO > 1.0% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above 3% over two consecutive quarters signals strengthening aggregate demand, which boosts corporate revenue growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 rises by > 3.0% for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of two consecutive quarterly GDPC1 rises > 3.0% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4% over two consecutive months combined with a decline in payroll employment below 150,000 new jobs per month over the same period signals a dual labor market weakening, which reduces consumer demand and corporate earnings, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 4.0 for two consecutive months AND PAYEMS < 150,000 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods where UNRATE > 4.0 and PAYEMS < 150,000 for two consecutive months (t-test p > 0.05).
